full_judgment:
Latifur Rahman J: This appeal by the complainant-appellant is against the judgment and order dated 4th December, 1997 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division making the Rule absolute in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 598 of 1995 quashing the proceedings of Complaint Case No. 135 of 1994 pending in the Court of Senior Special Judge and Sessions Judge, Dhaka. 

 2. An Officer of International Finance Investment and Commerce Bank Limited (IFIC), filed a petition of complaint against the accused-respondent alleging that while the respondent was serving as Manager at Gulshan Branch of the Bank he committed criminal offences during the course of his employment as public servant and misappropriated a total amount of Taka 26.18 crore causing huge loss to the Bank. Cognizance was taken and the trial was proceeding when the accused-respondent filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 598 of 1995 under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing of the said proceeding before the High Court Division on the grounds, inter alia, that he is not a public servant and, as such, the cognizance taken by the Special Judge on 5-9-94 under sections 409, 477A, 462A of the Penal Code and section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 was without jurisdiction, because a case against a private person cannot be filed under the said Act. 

 3. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute on the ground that the case filed upon a complaint under Act II of 1947 by a private individual is not maintainable. 

 Thus the accused who was a Manager of the IFIC Bank and the complainant who is an officer of the Bank are public servants, as it is a Banking Company whose 40% shares are held by the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. So both the complainant and the accused are public servants and the complaint has been filed before the Senior Special Judge and Sessions Judge, Dhaka for taking cognizance under sections 409, 477A and 462A of the Penal Code and under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 for misappropriating an amount of Taka 26.18 crore causing huge loss to the Bank. Section 110 of Banking Companies Act, 1991 also provides that a Manager, Officer and other functionaries of the banking company are deemed to be public servants under section 21 of the Penal Code. Thus, by reference to the relevant law we hold that the appellant and the respondent are public servants and the case has been rightly instituted in the court of Special Judge against the respondent who is also a public servant. 

 9. Further, section 5 of Act II of 1947 speaks of the offences as mentioned in the schedule of the Act to be tried by Special Judges. In the schedule we find sections 403 and 477A of the Penal Code with which the accused has been charged for committing misconduct as a public servant. In the case of Mahbubul Alam vs State reported in 50 DLR (AD) 125 we have already held as follows: 

 The accused petitioner being a Public Servant he was proceeded with under section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 and this, in fact, gave jurisdiction to the Special Judge to try the petitioner as an accused in the Special case. The learned Single Judge was totally wrong in holding that the accused petitioner cannot be tried under Act II of 1947 along with other Penal Code offence. Hence, this observation of the learned Single Judge is not correct in law.
